label: PF Backlog 5
title: WG-O5: Assign a SPECIFIC backlog item to a session/worker (claim-by-id + operator assignment) with lease semantics
body: Part of EPIC BI-PF-0360. Source: docs/WORKER-SCHEDULER-OPERATIONS.md.

brief.problem: claim is next-eligible only; cannot hand a specific item to a specific session for parallel work.
brief.what_adds: Claim-by-item-id and operator assignment endpoints, reusing the existing lease/heartbeat/complete lifecycle.
brief.why: Enables deliberate parallel work: each session gets a chosen item, with leases still preventing overlap.

objective: Support claiming/assigning a specific item id (not just next-eligible).
acceptance_criteria: POST assignments/claim accepts an optional item_id; eligibility + lease rules enforced identically.
An operator can assign item X to worker Y (audited).
Double-claim is still impossible; blocked/ineligible items are rejected fail-closed.
wg CLI exposes the by-id claim.
approach: Extend claim_next with an item_id path; add an operator assign endpoint; reuse lease lifecycle.
verification: claim a specific eligible item; blocked item rejected; second claim denied.

analysis.implementation_strategy: Extend core/backlog.py with a claim-by-id operation exposing claim ownership + lease expiry; add REST endpoint POST /api/v1/backlog/items/{id}/claim (guarded, operator assignment via assignee override). Wire into core/worker.py session start so a worker can claim a specific item; release/expire logic reuses core/release.py lease patterns if present.
dependency_findings: REQUIRES BI-PF-1327 (worktree session model + API-only backlog writes guard) — claim endpoint must obey its write-guard allowlist.
RELATED BI-PF-1325 (PF_API_TOKEN) for auth on the new endpoint.
RELATED BI-PF-1326 (start-from-anywhere wrapper) will call claim-by-id.
conflict_findings: core/backlog.py also touched by BI-PF-1328 (children regeneration) only via config validation — low overlap.
BI-PF-1327's API-only writes guard touches the same REST layer; sequence after 1327 completes.
duplication_findings: No existing claim-by-id API; /api/v1/backlog/groom/approve and /api/v1/backlog/ids:reserve cover adjacent flows but not assignment+lease.
core/backlog_link.py handles item relations, not ownership — no overlap.
analysis.rationale: Operators need to pin a specific backlog item to a specific worker/session with safe lease semantics; this is the core scheduling primitive for the WG epic.
assumptions: BI-PF-1327's write guard exposes an allowlist that can include claim/checkpoint/delivery endpoints.
Lease model similar to existing worker lease in core/worker.py.
config/engineering-workers.json lists workers that can be assigned.
risks: Lease expiry vs session liveness mismatch could double-assign items.
Write-guard allowlist from BI-PF-1327 not yet defined may force rework of endpoint guard.
Operator assignment could conflict with a worker's in-flight claim — needs takeover policy.
evidence: Candidate components core/backlog.py, core/worker.py, core/release.py exist.
missing_info: Lease duration and renewal cadence for claims.
Takeover policy: can an operator force-reassign an active claim?
Scope of the BI-PF-1327 write-guard allowlist.

context_review.reason: Building blocks (backlog API, worker module, release patterns) exist; implementation blocked only on BI-PF-1327 interface details.

dependencies.required_state: API-only backlog writes guard with endpoint allowlist
start-from-anywhere wrapper ready to call claim
